title: Unrelated writer activity in another request wipes an owner's entire writer state
claim: writerPresent treats an odd writerVersion as a possible match and callers dirty the owner on TryLock failure, so any concurrent writer wrapper or Buffer hook in another request wipes all Builder/Buffer taint of an owner that is inside a writer critical section (399/400 lost vs 0/400 control).

title: strings.Builder view ABA after GC address reuse reports clean content as tainted
claim: Builder entries are validated only by numeric (pointer,len,cap) with no backing anchor; after an unwrapped reset/refill, GC reuses the address and a clean String() is published with stale taint.

title: Repeated String() on an unchanged tracked writer burns the request root budget
claim: Each String() on a tracked writer publishes a new root even when unchanged; after 511 calls the 512-root budget is exhausted and later provenance in the request is dropped.

title: The 4-owners-per-receiver limit is soft, and exceeding it wipes a whole owner
claim: updateWriter second loop can add a 5th owner for a receiver; the next lookup dirties that owner, wiping all its writers.

title: A dirty owner keeps stale entries, charges and the process fast gate until it next writes
claim: LookupWriterValue skips dirty owners so their entries and writerbridge.Active() persist until the owner next writes or finishes, keeping all bytes.Buffer hooks on the slow path.

title: Dirtying on lock failure is not counted
claim: These dirty paths do not increment drops.contention, hiding F1 from telemetry.
